belief: I'll have to take this forever, so I'll never really be well.
origins: Long-term medication for chronic conditions can feel like a life sentence. We equate “well” with “needing nothing,” and so we feel permanently broken even when we are doing well.
teaches: The apostle Paul prayed three times for his thorn to be removed. Instead, God said, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” People can live full, productive lives while managing a condition. David wrote, “I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” Wellness is not the absence of need but the presence of care, purpose, and peace. Needing daily help is one way to depend daily on God’s provision.
self_statements: I will always be a patient.
Being on medication means I am sick.
errors: Believing I am either medication-free and well or sick.
Feeling burdened and concluding I am never well.
questions: What parts of my life are going well because of this treatment?
Who do I know who lives fully with a long-term condition?
How could I see my medication as a daily provision?
What does Scripture say about grace in weakness?
What would help me feel more at peace with daily treatment?
truth: I can live well while managing a condition. Daily care is a provision and a reminder of God’s daily grace, not a sign that I am broken beyond hope.
hw_truths: His power is perfected in weakness.
I can live a full life with care.
Each day I can thank God for provision.
log: Each week, note three ways you are doing well.
actions: Write what a good day looks like.
Link medication to a daily habit.
Pair your dose with a short prayer.
Ask about long-term outlook and adjustments.
prayer: Lord, I am tired of daily medicine. Teach me to receive it as Your provision, and help me live fully and gratefully each day. Amen.
